messages:
isa: FYI new hire hit a hang in the Go quickstart using Generator.Stream in an HTTP handler. Repro with token rotation proxy and wrk.

mike: paste the handler? Common pitfall is using r.Context() for handshake + stream.

isa: minimal handler:
func StreamHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  stream, err := client.Generator("mini").Stream(r.Context(), prompt)
  if err != nil { http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500); return }
  defer stream.Close()
  for c := range stream.Chunks() { fmt.Fprint(w, c.Text) }
}

zoe: handshake may block on auth refresh. If request cancels, Close can wait on handshake and leak goroutines. Short-term: do handshake on background ctx with small timeout: hsCtx := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1200*time.Millisecond)

isa: tried thatit helps but mid-stream refresh failures still leak. New devs expect defer Close to always free resources.

mike: SDK proposal: expose StartStream(handshakeCtx, opts...) returning Receiver with Chunks() and Close() that preempts handshake. Also add docs/recipe for "streams in HTTP handlers".

qa-bot: created ticket DEVEX-632: go-sdk stream handshake ergonomics. Added repro scripts and CI flaky test request.

zoe: i'll prototype API and add a CI test that rotates tokens under load. If anyone else sees this, drop OS/go/sdk versions and minimal repro.
